note: ETF League (second league of the Arena). Fictional money, simulation only: no broker, no real orders, no advice. Rules frozen before the first live night; any change is logged in rules/changes.md and applies only going forward. Decisions at the close of the last trading day of each month (and once at day zero); orders fill at the next open. Technical rehearsal = the same rules replayed on past data; it is never evidence.

costs.note: 0.1% commission per order plus half of a conservative ETF spread paid on every fill (assumptions, to be checked against real broker price lists)

tax.note: 28% on net realised gains per calendar year, shown apart: the value in the table is before tax, 'after tax' subtracts it. Rate to be confirmed on the official tax authority site.

strategies.name: Equal-weight core
strategies.text: 1/N over World, Eurozone, Emerging, euro bonds, inflation-linked bonds, gold and cash
strategies.evidence: medium (DeMiguel et al. 2009: 1/N is hard to beat)

strategies.name: Risk parity
strategies.text: World, euro bonds, global bonds, inflation-linked bonds and gold weighted by 1 / 12-month volatility

strategies.name: Dual momentum
strategies.text: Best 12-month return among US, Eurozone, Emerging, Japan; if it does not beat cash, hold global bonds

strategies.name: 10-month trend, five assets
strategies.text: 1/5 each in US, Emerging, euro bonds, gold, World; a slice below its 10-month average moves to cash

strategies.name: 10-month trend, World only
strategies.text: World ETF while above its 10-month average, cash otherwise

strategies.name: Sector momentum
strategies.text: Top 3 of 5 sectors by 6-month return, equal weight; cash if World is below its 10-month average

strategies.name: Low volatility
strategies.text: The 5 equity ETFs (sectors excluded) with the lowest 12-month volatility, equal weight

strategies.name: Factor mix
strategies.text: Equal weight in Quality, Value and Small caps

strategies.name: All-asset momentum
strategies.text: Top 5 of the 20 risk assets by 12-1 month momentum; a slice with a negative 12-month return goes to cash
